title: All-Minors Matrix-Tree Theory for Superport Networks: Completed Quotient-Incidence Determinants and Conductance-Weighted Subdivision Extensions
summary: An electrical network can be summarized at its boundary by a response matrix: prescribed boundary voltages determine boundary currents. A superport network adds a constraint by grouping boundary terminals into superports, requiring the total current in each group to be zero and making voltage differences inside the groups the natural coordinates. Earlier work determined forest formulas for a single response entry and for the determinant of the whole response matrix.
